0.long_answer: Amiloride is a potassium-sparing diuretic that is commonly used to treat hypertension as well as lithium-induced and other forms of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. In this condition, the kidney is unable to concentrate urine due to reduced responsiveness to vasopressin. By sparing potassium and inhibiting sodium reabsorption in the distal tubule, amiloride helps reduce polyuria and improves urinary concentration. This mechanism makes it a first-line treatment option for patients with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, particularly when it is induced by lithium use.
